question: How can GAN training be made more stable and GAN samples and semi-supervised classifiers better, and how can sample quality be scored without human raters?
hypothesis: Heuristic techniques that encourage convergence of the GAN game (feature matching, minibatch discrimination, historical averaging, one-sided label smoothing, virtual batch norm) improve semi-supervised accuracy and sample quality.
contributions: Five training techniques: feature matching, minibatch discrimination, historical averaging, one-sided label smoothing, virtual batch normalization
Inception score as an automatic image-quality metric
Semi-supervised GAN with K+1 classifier, state of the art on MNIST, CIFAR-10, SVHN

method.summary: Techniques added to DCGAN-style generator/discriminator pairs. For semi-supervised learning the discriminator is a K+1 class classifier trained with supervised cross-entropy plus the GAN game loss, with the generator trained by feature matching. Evaluated on MNIST, CIFAR-10, SVHN and ImageNet, with MTurk and Inception score.
method.task: semi-supervised classification and image generation with GANs

datasets.name: MNIST (permutation invariant)
datasets.split: 20, 50, 100 or 200 labeled examples (balanced per class), rest unlabeled; 10 random subsets

datasets.name: SVHN
datasets.preprocessing: same architecture and setup as CIFAR-10

models.name: MNIST GAN
models.architecture: networks with 5 hidden layers each; weight normalization; Gaussian noise added to output of each discriminator layer

models.name: CIFAR-10 / SVHN GAN
models.architecture: discriminator: 9 layer CNN with dropout and weight normalization; generator: 4 layer CNN with batch normalization

models.name: ImageNet GAN
models.architecture: modified public DCGAN TensorFlow implementation, multi-GPU

training.objective: L = L_supervised + L_unsupervised (K+1 class cross-entropy; unsupervised part is the GAN game value); generator by feature matching ||E f(x) - E f(G(z))||^2 for semi-supervised, minibatch discrimination for samples
training.dropout: used in CIFAR-10 discriminator, rate not stated
training.regularisation: one-sided label smoothing (positive targets alpha, value not stated; examples .9), historical averaging, weight normalization, Gaussian noise on D layers (MNIST)
training.hardware: multi-GPU for ImageNet, number not stated
training.seeds: 10 random label subsets/splits per semi-supervised result

other.paper_defers: All code and hyperparameters at github.com/openai/improved_gan

metrics.name: Test errors (MNIST)
metrics.definition: number of incorrectly classified test examples

metrics.name: Inception score
metrics.definition: exp(E_x KL(p(y|x) || p(y))) using pretrained Inception

metrics.name: MTurk human error rate
metrics.definition: fraction of real/generated judgments annotators got wrong or right

eval.protocol: Semi-supervised results mean and std over 10 seeds/splits; ablations scored by Inception score on 50k samples; MTurk votes via web interface.

results.table: Table 2, row Our model, column 4000 (18.63+/-2.32); ensemble 15.59+/-0.47

results.claim: Ablation scores: -VBN+BN 7.54, -L+HA 6.86, -LS 6.83, -L 4.36; removing minibatch features hurts more than removing labels.
MTurk annotators distinguished minibatch-discrimination MNIST samples from real in 52.4% of cases.
results.quote: distinguish samples in 52.4% of cases (2000 votes total)

results.claim: MTurk users correctly categorized 78.7% of CIFAR-10 images from best model; falls to 71.4% on the top 1% by Inception score.
results.setup: CIFAR-10, 50% real 50% fake; authors themselves >95% accuracy
results.quote: MTurk users correctly categorized 78.7% of images correctly

results.claim: Inception score should be evaluated on large sample counts (50k) because part measures diversity.

limits: Inception score is a rough guide; directly optimizing it yields adversarial examples (authors).
Techniques are heuristic with no convergence guarantee; interaction between G and the classifier in semi-supervised learning not fully understood.
MTurk results depend on annotator motivation and feedback; authors beat MTurk with >95% accuracy.
ImageNet samples have incorrect anatomy; no quantitative ImageNet result.
Optimizer, learning rates, batch size, steps not given in the paper (deferred to code).
Inception score later criticised by other work (not in this paper).
